On-device text reading for recipe photos and scanned PDFs.
tesseract.js 7.0.0 (Apache License 2.0) - tesseract.esm.min.js (the package's module edition of tesseract.min.js, loaded with import()), worker.min.js, LICENSE-tesseract.js.md
Bundled inside those files (versions checked against npm): regenerator-runtime 0.13.11, buffer 6.0.3, base64-js 1.5.1, bmp-js 0.1.0, is-url 1.2.4 and zlibjs 0.3.1 (MIT), ieee754 1.2.1 (BSD-3-Clause), idb-keyval 6.2.1 and wasm-feature-detect 1.8.0 (Apache-2.0). Notices: tesseract.min.js.LICENSE.txt, worker.min.js.LICENSE.txt; full texts: THIRD-PARTY-LICENSES.txt
tesseract.js-core 7.0.0 (Apache License 2.0) - core/*.wasm.js, core/LICENSE
@tesseract.js-data/eng 1.0.0 - lang/eng.traineddata.gz (4.0.0_best_int). Data from tesseract-ocr/tessdata_best via naptha/tessdata, both Apache License 2.0: lang/LICENSE and lang/NOTICE.txt. The npm package metadata says MIT but ships no licence text.
Loaded only when someone reads a photo. Nothing leaves the device.
tesseract.js-core 7.0.0 engine files (core/) compile in the Tesseract OCR engine (5.1.0 development build), Leptonica, libjpeg 9a, libpng 1.6.38, zlib 1.2.12, libtiff, libwebp, giflib, openlibm and the Emscripten 4.0.15 runtime. Their notices: core/THIRD-PARTY-LICENSES.txt.
